# T6.05: one HEVC IDR from our own picture setup

`src/enc.c` has a codec switch (`EncConfig.codec = ENC_HEVC`), `encode1 -hevc` encodes one IDR, and `h264check`
decodes HEVC too (told apart by the first NAL unit: a VPS).

## What the HEVC path does

- **Methods**: `SET_APPLICATION_ID` 3 (`NVENC_H265`), `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS` codec type **4** (not in `clc9b7.h`; seen in
  nullmoth's library, T6.03), no colocated-data methods. Everything else as for H.264.
- **Picture setup** (`setup_hevc`): `nvenc_h265_drv_pic_setup_s` with our input/recon surfaces (as H.264, plus the
  half-plane field offsets nullmoth sets on ref/output surfaces), SPS data (CTB 32, CB 16..32, TB 4..32, depths 3/3,
  AMP, SAO, one short-term RPS), PPS data matching `hevc_write_pps`, constant-QP RC, `pic_control` with `codec` 5,
  `ceil_log2_pic_size_in_ctbs`, SAO modes 31, NAL type 19 (IDR) / 1, source padding, `qpfifo` 1, one slice control
  (all CTUs, `qp_avr`, slice type, SAO and loop-filter flags).
- **Controls**: `setup_me_hevc` / `setup_md_hevc` / `setup_q_hevc` set nullmoth's values by field
  (`docs/traces/vttest-hevc-256x128-controls.txt`), the same for IDR and P. `scripts/structdump.py` generates field
  printers for these structs (`tools/nvencdump.h`), and `tools/hevcsetup` uses them to compare setups field by field.
- **Buffers**: input planes cover whole 32-row CTBs; recon slots 64 KB larger than the planes (as nullmoth's; what the
  engine keeps there isn't known yet, T6.06).
- **Headers**: `enc_headers` writes VPS + SPS + PPS (`src/hevchdr.c`).

## The one thing that broke it: sign data hiding

The first IDR encoded without errors (microcode status 0) and decoded without errors, but at 10.3 dB. Isolating it:

| test | result | so |
|---|---|---|
| flat black / white picture | exact (138 dB) | the engine reads our input at the right place |
| one flat bright 16x16 block at (0,0) or (5,3) | exact | block positions are right |
| a 16x16 block with a ramp inside | wrong values everywhere after it, even in the flat background | not a pixel order problem: the decoder loses sync on the first coded residual |
| each coding tool off in setup and headers (`ENC_HEVC_OFF`) | only **sign data hiding off** fixes it (48.2 dB); transform skip, CU QP delta, SAO, AMP off or strong intra smoothing on change nothing | |

**NVENC does not apply sign data hiding**, even with `pps_data.sign_data_hiding_enabled_flag` set; a PPS that signals it
makes the decoder hide/infer signs the engine didn't. Our setup and PPS now leave it off (`HevcParams.no_sdh`).
nullmoth's library signals it too. Clearing the bit in their recorded PPS did not make their 256x128 stream decode
correctly, but their stream also carries the input layout problem, so that test doesn't decide anything for them.

## Result (256x128, `encode1 -hevc`, synthetic pattern)

| QP | bits | luma | chroma |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 23,160 | 57.5 dB | 62.8 dB |
| 18 | 12,976 | 52.1 dB | 54.6 dB |
| 25 | 7,600 | 48.2 dB | 49.6 dB |
| 32 | 5,024 | 43.8 dB | 44.8 dB |
| 40 | 3,296 | 37.2 dB | 40.3 dB |

H.264 at QP 25, same picture: 10,800 bits, 45.3 dB. All decode with 0 errors.

`ENC_HEVC_OFF=ts,cqd,sao,amp,sis` stays as an experiment switch for the next tasks.
